‘The video-output circuit consists of three individual circuits: Xaxis, Y-axis, and Z-axis. The X-axis and Y-axis video-output circuits each consist of a digtal-to-analog converter (DAC), current-to-voltage converter, two sample and holds, and amplifier. The Z-axis, Video-output ci X and Y Outputs ‘The DACs (011 and 811) each receive binary numbers from the vector generator’s pos: tion counter outputs. These numbers represent the location of the beam on the monitor. For the nominverted X axis, the numbers range from 0 to 1023, where Ois atthe far lett of tthe monitor screen, $12 atthe center, and 1023 is atthe far right. For the non-inverted ¥ axis, the numbers range from 128 to 996, where 128 Is at the bottom of the monitor screen, 512's at the center, and 996 is at the top. When the X axis and Y axis are inverted, the monitor picture is tumed upside down. This is used for a two-player cocktail game: ‘The DACs convert these binary number inputs to current outputs. The DACs! current ‘outputs are applied to the pin-6 inputs of current-tovoltage converters C12 and A12. From the current-o-voltage converters, the signal is fed to two sample-and hold circuits: ‘One is non- inverted and the other is inverted. The non-inverted sample and hold consists ‘of one stage of analog switch D12 and capacitor C89 forthe X axis, and B12 and C109 for the Y axis. The inverting sample and hold consists of inverter E12, one stage of analog switch D2, and capacitor C88 for the X axis and BICI2, B12 and CHO for the Y axis ‘The sampleand.hold circuits are controlled by SHCON (sample and hold contro}. 'SHCON is derived by gating 3 MHz from the microcomputer clock circultry and VGCK* from the vector generator's state generator. The result of these inputs insures that the rnor-inverted and inverted analog signals that are applied tothe analog switches have sutficiently stabilized before being applied to the sample-and-hold capacitors.

‘The output swing of SHCON Is ~8 to +8 VOC. When SHCON is high, the voltage: charges or discharges the sample-and-hold capacitors to the X and Y analog voltage value. The voltages are then applied to the inputs of the second analog switch. These Switches select either the non inverted or inverted X-axis and Y-axis outputs. The outputs are then amplified by the second stages of C12 and A12 for an impedance-matched outbut to the X and ¥ inputs to the monitor. Since the monitor doesn't have fieldadjustable X and Y gains, the gains are adjustable by variable resistors F120 and R128. Z Output ‘The Z-axis video output receives six inputs. BVLD (beam valid), from the output of the vector generator’s position counters, tells the Z axis to draw the line. BLANK (vector ine blank), trom the vector generator’s state machine, tells the Z axis to stop drawing alin.
